title: rwb-access sandbox seed: the access seed file's location, format, version label and row count are not specified, and whether the DEV matrix version must equal the SIT version is not stated
source: Legacy RWB-E1-065 sections 3, 4 step 8, 11 and 13; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.3 and A2.4 AC-P4-004-01; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1 (permission.matrix_version) and T3.2; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 DP-07 and DP-15
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 7 AC1 and AC2; section 8 BR10; section 13 Configuration and reference data and Database and migrations
description: Three values this slice needs are absent. (1) The legacy story names the seed file only as 'roles.txt, Permissions' in its preconditions and as 'the roles.txt seed file' in section 13, with no repository path, no format, no owner and no row count; the 54-role count appears in flow step 8 but no source enumerates the permission rows the file carries. (2) The matrix version label the sandbox must write is given only as an example in the FSD (matrix file PM-2026.12 with 756 rows, loaded and approved by a security administrator), not as the label of the DEV seed. (3) Legacy BR2 requires the sandbox to be built from the same DDL as SIT, but no source says whether the DEV access seed must also carry the same matrix version as the one in force in SIT.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-065 section 3 reads 'The role to permission matrix rows (roles.txt, Permissions) are available as a seed file for the sandbox' and section 13 reads 'roles and permissions from the roles.txt seed file', with no path and no version; flow step 8 reads 'loads the 54 roles, the permission matrix and one named test user per role'; FSD P4 A2.4 AC-P4-004-01 loads 'matrix file PM-2026.12' with 756 rows as an example of a running load; TSD P4 T3.1 gives permission.matrix_version varchar(20) with no value and no list; no extract names the DEV seed's label or its path.
area: rwb-access access seed and matrix version
proposed: Fix the seed file in the rwb-access repository as a migration resource with a stated path and format, publish its version label and row count with RWB-P4-E1037-CON, and state in the Service Contract Catalog whether the DEV seed carries the matrix version in force in SIT or a DEV-only label.

title: rwb-access sandbox seed: the owner, the key format and the retirement rule of the DEV synthetic test identity per role are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-065 sections 3, 4 step 8, 8 BR6 and 10; Business Requirements Epic 1 v4 DL39; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.3 field catalog (v_ace_iam_group.entra_group); TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1 (role.entra_group DF-REF-039) and T6.2
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 7 AC3; section 8 BR2; section 10 Authority; section 13 Configuration and reference data
description: Legacy BR6 and DL39 require every role to have a test user before it has real users, and legacy flow step 8 loads 'one named test user per role'. The target has no table for a test identity: TSD P4 defines role.entra_group as the Entra ID group mapped to the role and states it is read from ACE (iam_group, RWB-ACE-001), while the sign-in path is owned by other P4 stories. Who owns the DEV identity list, what the identity key looks like, where the identity is created (directory account or seeded row) and when it is retired are absent from every source read.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-065 BR6 reads 'Every role has a named test user before it has real users | DL39'; its flow step 8 and solution-plan component AccessSeedLoader read 'one named test user per role'; FSD P4 A2.3 and A2.4 field catalogs read 'v_ace_iam_group.entra_group | Entra ID group mapped to the role, read from ACE (iam_group, RWB-ACE-001); not a Workbench column'; TSD P4 T3.1 gives role.entra_group with source 'Entra ID' and no identity table exists in T3.1.
proposed: Assign the DEV identity list to the platform administrator, fix the synthetic key format in the Service Template Specification, record the retirement rule with DL39, and state in the sign-in story (RWB-P4-E1022-APP) that the identity resolves to role.entra_group rows only.

title: rwb-access sandbox seed: the per-service login name and the DEV-only read-only role over rwb_access are not fixed for the target schema
source: Legacy RWB-E1-065 sections 3, 4 step 10, 10 and 13; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T6.2; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 20, 41 and 42; DP-02 and DP-15
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 7 AC8; section 8 BR9; section 10 Authority; section 13 Configuration and reference data
description: The legacy story grants SELECT on the single recovery schema to a DEV role named rwb_sandbox_read, mapped to the Entra group RWB-DEV-RW-TRIBE. In the target the sandbox is split per service schema, so the read-only role must be scoped to rwb_access, and no source states whether the legacy role name survives, whether it is granted on the seed tables only, and whether it may read the access log. The per-service login of rwb-access is also unnamed; the service table fixes the schema name only.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-065 section 3 reads 'The Entra ID group RWB-DEV-RW-TRIBE exists and maps to the sandbox read-only database role', section 4 step 10 reads 'grants SELECT on schema recovery to role rwb_sandbox_read', section 10 gives RW-TRIBE 'Read and extract the sandbox through role rwb_sandbox_read', and section 13 repeats the grant; Architecture v5 slide 41 fixes schema rwb_access with 'its own login' and names no login; TSD P4 T6.2 names no login and no read-only role; DP-02 leaves the login name to the platform DB story.
proposed: Fix the rwb-access login in the platform DB story, publish the DEV-only read-only role and its grant list (SELECT on role and permission only, no access-entry read) in the Service Template Specification, and record the retirement of the single-schema grant with DP-15.

title: rwb-access sandbox seed: the authorise and me/permissions request and answer shapes, and the screen route that shows the seeded rows, are absent from the TSD appendix
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 41; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T-A.1 and T6.1; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.4, A2.7 and Screens; Legacy RWB-E1-065 section 12
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 7 AC3 to AC5; section 12.1 and 12.8 Contract; section 13 Build steps 5 and 6; section 15 Screens and states
description: Three values are absent. (1) Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41 name POST /authorise and GET /me/permissions as the first API paths of rwb-access, but the TSD P4 appendix T-A endpoint inventory holds neither path and defines no request or answer schema, so the fields this story answers with (decision code, matrix version, letters per area, scope, entry reference) and the fields a caller sends are a read. (2) The legacy story names one endpoint used in DEV against the sandbox (GET on the case list, refused with MSG-P4-002 for a role without the right) and no authorise call, so the shape is carried by the target contract rather than the legacy story. (3) The gateway-bff composite route behind SCR-43 Roles and access has no field list and no hop list (DP-19).
evidence: Arch v5 slide 41 gives rwb-access the first API path /authorise and slide 14 lists 'POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA) · GET /me/permissions · GET /doa-limits · /masking-policies' as IN; TSD P4 T-A.1 lists API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 and none is the authorise or me/permissions path; TSD P4 T3.1 defines no authorise object; Legacy RWB-E1-065 section 12 holds one row, 'GET ... /cases', with no authorise call; FSD P4 Screens lists SCR-43 with no route detail.
proposed: Add the two paths with their request and answer schema to the API specification and TSD P4 appendix T-A, publish them with RWB-P4-E1037-CON and stub them in that contract fake, and publish the composite route of SCR-43 with gateway-bff (DP-19).

title: rwb-access sandbox seed: the legacy seed loads 54 roles, while the TSD P4 RBAC matrix tabulates 42 role rows, and the difference is not enumerated
source: Legacy RWB-E1-065 section 4 step 8 and section 10; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T6.1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 P4 (Recovery roles as data)
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 7 AC1 and AC3; section 8 BR4; section 13 Configuration and reference data
description: The legacy sandbox loads 54 roles. The TSD P4 RBAC matrix tabulates 42 rows: 37 RW- roles and 5 SY- roles. The 12 roles present in the seed and absent from the matrix are not named anywhere, and no source says which count the target seed must carry, so the role count and the identity count this story asserts cannot both be grounded in one source.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-065 flow step 8 reads 'loads the 54 roles, the permission matrix and one named test user per role'; TSD P4 T6.1 runs from 'RW-CASEOWN Case owner' to 'SY-AGENT Agent platform' in 42 rows; no extract lists a 54-role set or names the 12 extra roles.
proposed: Publish the 54-role list in the Service Contract Catalog with the administration and non-human roles marked, reconcile it with the 42 tabulated rows in T6.1, and fix the role count the DEV seed carries.

title: rwb-access sandbox seed: the matrix letters for 11 of the 14 capability areas are not tabulated, so the seed content has no source table
source: TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T6.1 and T3.2 (LOV-CAPABILITY); FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.4 AC-ALT-P4-004-02 and AC-P4-007-01; Legacy RWB-E1-065 sections 3 and 7 AC1
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 7 AC1, AC4 and AC5; section 8 BR6; section 13 Build steps 1 and 3
description: The TSD P4 RBAC matrix tabulates three capability areas only (Rules and parameters, Reference data, Platform administration), while LOV-CAPABILITY holds 14. The letters for CASE_RECORD, QUEUE_AND_ALLOCATION, TREATMENT_AND_OFFER, LITIGATION, ASSET_AND_DISPOSAL, DEBT_SALE, WRITE_OFF_AND_POSTING, DOCUMENTS, DECISION_LOG, PARTNER_PORTAL and REPORTING for any role are absent from every table read, so the matrix rows this seed writes come from the legacy seed file, which is not in the extracts. The refusal in the legacy access case depends on exactly this: RW-REFADM holds no CASE_RECORD row.
evidence: TSD P4 T6.1 column headers read 'Rules and parameters | Reference data | Platform administration' only, and LOV-CAPABILITY in T3.2 lists 14 areas; FSD P4 A2.4 AC-ALT-P4-004-02 refuses RW-CASEOWN a QUEUE_AND_ALLOCATION U right, which shows letters exist per area beyond the three columns; FSD P4 A2.7 AC-P4-007-01 has RW-CASEOWN read a case, which shows a CASE_RECORD R letter exists; Legacy RWB-E1-065 section 7 TC-E1-065-10 has RW-REFADM refused the case list and section 3 supplies the matrix only as 'roles.txt, Permissions'.
proposed: Extend the T6.1 matrix to the 14 capability areas of LOV-CAPABILITY and publish the full matrix version with the pack load story RWB-P4-AD002-APP; until then carry the letters of the remaining areas in the seed file only, with default deny where a row is absent.

title: rwb-access ACE masking pack: no source names which ACE view fields the masking rows must cover or at which field IDs
source: Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 (DF-ACE-055 to DF-ACE-074 for v_ace_customer); TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T3.1 and the personal-data note; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1 (masking_rule); FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.5; Legacy RWB-E1-069 sections 7, 11 and 17
section: Section 2 Business rationale; section 3 Preconditions; section 7 Acceptance criteria; section 11 Data; section 13 Configuration and reference data
description: The masking pack has to hold one masking_rule row per personal field ID and role, but no source lists the ACE-sourced personal fields that the pack must cover. The dictionary gives the field IDs (v_ace_customer is DF-ACE-055 to DF-ACE-074, with DF-ACE-073 id_no_masked and DF-ACE-074 id_no_last4), and TSD P1 says the clear identity number is never exposed and that phone, email and address are exposed in full for notices and calls, which means the 'personal' flags of the dictionary and the masking obligation do not coincide one to one. The story therefore fixes the v_ace_customer range as the covered set and leaves the remaining 29 views to a pack decision no source records.
evidence: TSD P4 T3.1 defines masking_rule with role_code, field_id, unmasked and masking_version but names no field list; FSD P4 A2.5 gives no field catalogue; the v_ace_customer rows exist in the dictionary with their field IDs, while the other 29 views carry no pack instruction; TSD P1 T3.1 says phone, email and address are exposed in full, which conflicts with treating every dictionary-personal field as masked by default.
proposed: Publish the masking field map as part of the pack design: one row per personal field ID of the 30 views with the role that may see it, agreed by the Compliance and PDPA officer, and load it with the pack instead of leaving the set to the story.

title: rwb-access ACE masking pack: no source names the masking version label
source: TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1 (masking_version, varchar(20)) and T3.2 (LOV-VERSION-STATUS); FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.4 and A2.5 (MASK-SIT-01 in an acceptance example); Legacy RWB-E1-069 sections 12 and 13
section: Section 2 Business rationale; section 3 Preconditions; section 7 Acceptance criteria; section 12.1 Contract; section 13 Configuration and reference data
description: Every masking_rule row and every masking answer names a masking version, and the migration has to write the label of the version in force. No source fixes a label: the FSD uses 'MASK-SIT-01' inside an acceptance example for the SIT environment only, and TSD P4 defines the column without a format or a naming rule. This story uses MASK-2026.12, the label the Work Package fixes, and the real label has to come from the pack owner at load time.
evidence: TSD P4 T3.1 gives masking_version as varchar(20) with no format; FSD P4 AC-EXC-P4-004-05 and AC-EXC-P4-005-05 mention 'MASK-SIT-01' as an environment example; the legacy story names no version because it has no masking rows at all.
proposed: Fix the masking version naming rule with the pack owner (year and month, as the matrix version PM-2026.12 does) and record it in TSD P4 T3.1, so a migration never invents a label.

title: rwb-access ACE masking pack: no source holds the roster of roles that see a personal field unmasked
source: TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1 (masking_rule.unmasked) and T6.1 (RBAC matrix for three columns only); FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.5 and AC-EXC-P4-004-05; NFR-039 and NFR-040; Legacy RWB-E1-069 sections 10 and 17
section: Section 2 Business rationale; section 3 Preconditions; section 7 Acceptance criteria AC2 and AC3; section 8 Business rules BR2 and BR6; section 10 Authority
description: The masking answer depends on which roles see which personal field unmasked, and no source holds that roster. masking_rule is defined as data with an unmasked flag, FSD A2.5 says the fields are hidden from any role whose permission row does not allow them, and the TSD RBAC matrix tabulates only Rules and parameters, Reference data and Platform administration, so no Case record or Treatment and offer column exists to read a masking right from. The roster is therefore a pack decision: this story treats a row with unmasked true as the only allow, masks every other role, and never derives a clear answer from a permission letter.
evidence: TSD P4 T6.1 tabulates three columns and no personal-data column; FSD P4 A2.5 states the rule but names no role; the only role-shaped masking evidence in the sources is the example 'RW-PHONECOL sees the identity number as XXXXXXXXX1234' in FSD AC-ALT-P4-004-01, which fixes a masked rendering for one role and no unmasked role at all.
proposed: Publish the roster with the pack: for each personal field ID, the roles that see it unmasked, approved by the Compliance and PDPA officer and the security administrator, and hold it as masking_rule rows rather than in a matrix column.

title: rwb-access: the per-service database login name is named by no source
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 20 and 41; DP-02; Legacy RWB-E1-069 section 3 (roles ace_view_owner and recovery_svc)
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 10 Authority; section 13 Configuration and reference data
description: The legacy story names the two roles of the monolith, ace_view_owner and recovery_svc, and the target gives every service one login of its own. The platform DB story has not fixed the per-service login names, so this story cannot name the account it asserts AC8 against. It uses 'the rwb-access login (DP-02)' as a placeholder and names no credential.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 41 gives rwb-access schema rwb_access with its own login but no account name; DP-02 says one login per service; the legacy story's roles are the monolith's, and RWB-P1-E1069-DB owns the grants of the target.
owner_role: ACE team lead and ACE DBA
proposed: Fix the 19 per-service login names in the platform DB story and in the Environment and Deployment Design, and replace the placeholder in the privilege test of this story with the fixed name.

title: rwb-access: unclear whether this service may hold masking rows that key on the P1 field catalogue
source: Ownership Map (sys_objects, sys_fields and the dictionary owned by P1); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 (P4 owns the masking policy, P1 owns the ACE view contract); TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1 (masking_rule.field_id); Legacy RWB-E1-069 BR5
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 11 Data; section 12.7 Tables owned
description: masking_rule.field_id is a varchar(16) that carries a dictionary field ID, and the dictionary itself (sys_objects, sys_fields, sys_field_version) is P1's. No source says whether a masking row may reference another service's metadata, whether the reference may be a foreign key, or whether rwb-access must copy the field label. The story takes the narrow reading: the field ID is a key in this service's own table, there is no foreign key across schemas (DP-01), no dictionary row is copied and rwb-access reads no P1 table.
evidence: TSD P4 T3.1 gives field_id as varchar(16) with no reference; the Ownership Map gives sys_fields and sys_objects to P1; Architecture v5 slide 41 gives P4 the masking policy and P1 the ACE view contract; DP-01 forbids a cross-schema read.
proposed: Record in TSD P4 and in the physical schema note that masking_rule.field_id is a dictionary field ID held as a value with no cross-schema key, and confirm that the dictionary stays with P1's data-dictionary API and is not duplicated.

title: rwb-access: the boundary rule has no allowed-object list and no build-log wording for this service
source: Legacy RWB-E1-069 BR8, AC8, section 12 and section 14 (recovery-modules.yaml sourceViews and the BND-6 build log text); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 9 and 13 (only rwb-source-data reads the views); TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T1
section: Section 5 Exception paths X4 and X5; section 13 Components and Build steps; section 14 Validation and messages
description: The legacy rule reads its allowed view names from recovery-modules.yaml and fails a class that names a public table with a fixed sentence. In the target the module map is per service, and no source says what rwb-access's map holds, whether the rule also has to refuse the 30 view names for this service, or what the failure text says when the named object is a view rather than a public table. The story takes the empty allow-list reading: the map holds no source object, and the rule refuses both a view and a public table.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-069 section 13 gives recovery-modules.yaml the sourceViews list for the monolith module; Architecture v5 slide 9 says only rwb-source-data reads the views; TSD P4 T1 describes the service without a boundary list; no target document holds a per-service module map.
proposed: Publish the per-service module map with an explicitly empty source-object list for the 18 services that read no view, and fix the BND-6 failure wording once in the service template so every service reads the same sentence.

title: rwb-access plan status: the TSD RBAC matrix has no Case record column, so the CASE_RECORD letters this slice decides are not tabulated for any role
source: TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T6.1, T3.2 and T6.2; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.4 and A2.14; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 41; Legacy RWB-E2-002 sections 10 and 14
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 7 Background and AC1 to AC6; section 8 Business rules BR1 and BR2; section 13 Configuration and reference data
description: The legacy story names RW-CASEOWN, RW-RESTRUCT and RW-DATASTEW/RW-PLATADM in its authority table and gives every read the Case record R right, and FSD A2.4 defines the matrix over the 14 capability areas of LOV-CAPABILITY, which includes CASE_RECORD. The TSD P4 RBAC matrix tabulates three columns only - Rules and parameters, Reference data and Platform administration - and gives no letter for any role in Case record, so the letters this capability decides (CASE_RECORD R for RW-CASEOWN, RW-RESTRUCT and RW-AUDIT, and the absence of a CASE_RECORD row for RW-REFADM) are carried by the policy pack read in this story and not by a source table. The default scope of each role beyond RW-CASEOWN and RW-AUDIT is likewise not stated for Case record.
evidence: TSD P4 T6.1 rows run 'RW-CASEOWN Case owner | R | R | -' to 'SY-AGENT Agent platform | R | R | -' with the three column headers only, and the extra table for rule package and Temporal workflows refines no fourth area; LOV-CAPABILITY in T3.2 lists CASE_RECORD; FSD P4 A2.4 AC-ALT-P4-004-02 refuses RW-CASEOWN the QUEUE_AND_ALLOCATION U right, which shows the matrix is per area, while no Case record letter appears anywhere in T6.1; Legacy RWB-E2-002 section 10 gives 'RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Reads the plan status on cases in scope (Case record, R)' and section 14 carries MSG-P4-002 for the role without it.
proposed: Extend the T6.1 matrix with a Case record column for all roles, publish the full 14-area matrix version as data with RWB-P4-AD002-APP, and confirm the CASE_RECORD letters and the default scope of RW-CASEOWN, RW-RESTRUCT, RW-AUDIT and RW-REFADM with the matrix owner before PM-2026.12 goes in force.

title: rwb-access plan status: the authorise request and answer shapes and the resolved permission view are absent from the TSD P4 appendix, including whether the plan reference travels in the authorise request
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 20 and 41; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T-A.1, T6.2 and T3.1; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.4, A2.7 and A2.14; Legacy RWB-E2-002 sections 10, 12 and 14
section: Section 1 Story; section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 2, 4 and 12; section 8 Business rules BR2 and BR8; section 12.1, 12.2 and 12.8 Contract; section 13 Build step 1
description: Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41 name POST /authorise the first API path of rwb-access, with GET /me/permissions, GET /doa-limits and /masking-policies, and DP-08 makes authorise the contract every service asks before a read or an action. The TSD P4 appendix T-A.1 has no authorise path and no /me/permissions path: its nearest entry is API-P4-012 GET /me/session, which the TSD describes as the caller's resolved session with roles, scope and matrix and conflict versions, and API-P4-007 GET /admin/roles, which lists roles with permissions and scope for Platform administration R. No source fixes the fields the caller sends (identity, capability area, right, case reference, plan reference, field IDs, the owner, queue and team attributes for the scope test) or the fields the answer returns (decision code, matrix version, scope result, entry reference); in particular nothing states whether a plan-status read carries the plan reference TDR-SYN-0310 in the request, and the field IDs DF-CAS-046, DF-CAS-047 and DF-CAS-048 are named by the legacy data table only.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 41 gives rwb-access the first API path /authorise; slide 14 lists the P4 IN line 'REST POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA) - GET /me/permissions - GET /doa-limits - /masking-policies'; TSD P4 T-A.1 lists API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 and none of them is the authorise path or /me/permissions, and T-A.2 API-P4-012 (GET /me/session) answers 'the caller's resolved session: roles, scope, matrix and conflict versions, partner and break-glass state' with no field table; T3.1 defines no authorise object; Legacy RWB-E2-002 section 10 names roles and rights but no request shape, and section 12 carries only the monolith plan-status row.
proposed: Add the authorise path and the resolved permission view to the API specification and to TSD P4 appendix T-A with their request and answer schemas, publish them with RWB-P4-E1037-CON, stub them in that contract fake, and record whether the plan reference is part of the authorise request; keep GET /me/session as the session read of its own story.

title: rwb-access plan status: the per-service login name and the gateway-bff composite route field list behind SCR-03 and the plan status panel are not specified
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 10, 11, 20, 41 and 43; DP-02 and DP-19; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T6.2; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.30 and the Screens table; Legacy RWB-E2-002 section 15
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 10 Authority; section 12.1 Contract; section 13 Configuration and reference data; section 15 Screens and states
description: Two values this slice needs are absent. (1) The per-service database login for rwb-access is named nowhere; DP-02 requires one login per service and the story uses 'the rwb-access login (DP-02)' as a placeholder. (2) The gateway-bff composite route that serves SCR-03 Case record and its plan status panel has no published field list, hop list, merge order or field-level masking rule (DP-19); the FSD Screens table lists SCR-43 Roles and access and no case record screen, and the legacy story names SCR-03 and SCR-14 only, so the panel fields - the plan reference, the status and the status date - are known from the legacy story and the field-level composition of the route is not.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 41 requires one schema and one login per service and gives no name; slide 20 gives gateway-bff the browser entry and the parallel owner calls with a 2 s timeout; slide 10 shows the composite read of a case as two parallel calls merged at the gateway, with no field list; DP-19 in Template and Rules section R5.5 adds the composite route with H RWB-PLT-N001-CON and no schema; FSD P4 Screens lists SCR-39, SCR-40, SCR-41, SCR-42, SCR-43 and SCR-47 only; Legacy RWB-E2-002 section 15 says 'SCR-03 Case record, states loading and read only: the plan status panel shows the plan reference, status, date and, when not live, MSG-P2-008'.
proposed: Fix the rwb-access login in the platform DB story, and publish the composite route of SCR-03 with gateway-bff (DP-19) with its field list, its merge order and its masking rule; until then the story names the login by role and states which three fields the panel carries.

title: The roster of roles that see the other-products account number unmasked is an assumption of the legacy story
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5/RWB E2 003 Customer s other products on the case v1.md, sections 3 and 10; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.5; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1 (masking_rule)
description: The legacy story names the roster that sees v_ace_party_product.account_no clear and marks it assumed: RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-RESTRUCT, RW-SPECIAL and RW-GUARANT clear, the last four digits for every other role. No FSD, TSD or BRD row fixes that roster for this field, and the masking_rule table carries no seed rows. This story therefore writes the roster as data at masking version MASK-2026.12 and records it as an assumption.
evidence: Legacy section 3: 'The masking rules for v_ace_party_product.account_no are loaded (DL26; assumed: unmasked for RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-RESTRUCT, RW-SPECIAL and RW-GUARANT, masked to the last four digits for every other role).' Legacy section 10 row 2 carries '(assumed; DL26)'.
proposed: Confirm the five clear roles and that every other role holding Case record R is masked, then load the roster through the masking load path of RWB-P4-AD004-APP.

title: No source fixes the masking version label in force for the wave-2 release, or the rule for two valid versions on one day
source: TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1 (masking_version, valid_from, valid_to) and T3.2; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 AC-EXC-P4-004-05 and AC-ALT-P4-004-01 (MASK-SIT-01 example); legacy RWB-E2-003
description: masking_rule is versioned by masking_version with validity dates, but no source names the masking version in force at the 31 December 2026 release: the FSD examples use MASK-SIT-01 for SIT and the matrix uses PM-2026.x. The same silence leaves open which version answers when two rows are valid for the same field and business date. This story uses MASK-2026.12 as the wave-2 label and the latest valid_from on or before the business date as the rule, and the answer always names the version it used.
